title: Cron-Based "State Repairs" of Concurrency Deadlocks
pattern: Using a periodic background job/scheduler task to forcibly reset lock states, queues, or process flows because of latent deadlocks or hung transactions.
why_bad: Masks the root cause of concurrency bugs (deadlocks, race conditions, or leaks) rather than fixing them. It introduces non-deterministic behavior and risks severe data corruption.
detection: Periodic background threads or timer jobs that write to synchronization variables, reset state queues, or force-unlock mutexes to "unclog" execution paths.
counterexample: Legitimate periodic cleanup of historical, persisted logs or expired temporary storage.
fix: Identify and resolve the underlying deadlock/leak using RAII guards and proper lock ordering.
source: *Clean Code*, Appendix A: Concurrency II, "Deadlock," p. 332.
